title: Benchmark playback, annotations and alerting protocol
creator: Lina Park
description: Goal: Create a reproducible benchmark playback feature and an annotation/alerting protocol to accelerate triage of performance regressions (tokens/sec, latency p95, and throughput anomalies). This ticket covers: (1) storage schema updates to persist rolling-window token-level traces and deterministic workload seeds; (2) a playback engine that can reconstruct request timelines for a chosen model commit + workload + seed; (3) UI affordances to step through token emission, view KV cache hits/misses, and pin annotations to tokens or time ranges; (4) automated alert enrichment that classifies likely root causes (scheduling, kernel selection, batching contention, input distribution shift) and surfaces reproducible playback links to on-call and the incident runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Schema change accepted and migration plan documented: rolling-window traces (token-level events) stored for 30 days, aggregated rollups stored for 1 year
Playback engine implemented that can replay a stored run deterministically given model commit + workload id + seed
UI includes a playback timeline, token stepper, KV cache visualization, ability to attach annotations and tags to timestamp ranges
Automated alert enrichment attaches a playback link and a suggested root-cause label for >80% of regression alerts in internal test runs
Integration tests cover end-to-end: synthetic regression injected -> alert fired -> playback link reproduces anomaly on staging
implementation_notes: Storage: extend benchmark result bucket with a 'trace_events' table keyed by (model_commit, workload_id, seed, run_id, timestamp) and sharded by model_commit hash
Retention: compact token events into second-level aggregates for long-term storage, keep full token stream for recent 30 days for quick replay
Playback engine: lightweight deterministic runner in Go that can consume trace_events and reconstruct request/response timelines and simulated GPU scheduling boundaries
UI: reuse the existing regression-alert UI wiring but add a 'Replay' modal. Add stepper controls (+/- token, speed, goto timestamp) and KV cache panel showing key insert/eviction events
Alert enrichment: rule-based first pass (e.g., sudden p95 spike with unchanged QPS => likely kernel change) plus a simple classifier trained on historical triages to suggest labels
Security: playback links must be pre-signed and require a console token; full request payloads redacted unless run is marked as 'secure' and the user has KMS access
Perf: ensure trace ingestion adds <5% overhead to benchmark harness; use async upload with backpressure and batching
Observability: expose metrics for trace ingestion latency, playback render time, and annotation save rate
